london: London is on GMT (UTC+0) in winter and BST (UTC+1) from the last Sunday in March to the last Sunday in October. Greenwich, the reference point for GMT, is in south-east London.
new-york: New York uses Eastern Time: EST (UTC−5) in winter and EDT (UTC−4) from the second Sunday in March to the first Sunday in November. Many people write EST all year, so check the date when an exact time matters.
tokyo: Japan has a single time zone, JST (UTC+9), and has not used daylight saving since the early 1950s. The gap with Tokyo changes only when the other city changes its clocks.
los-angeles: Los Angeles uses Pacific Time: PST (UTC−8) in winter and PDT (UTC−7) in summer. San Francisco, Seattle and Las Vegas keep the same clock.
paris: France uses CET (UTC+1) and CEST (UTC+2), changing on the last Sundays of March and October. Counting its overseas territories, France spans 12 time zones, more than any other country, but this page covers mainland France.
dubai: Dubai uses Gulf Standard Time (UTC+4) all year. The UAE federal government moved to a Monday to Friday week with a half day on Friday in January 2022, so Friday afternoon is a poor time for a call.
sydney: Sydney uses AEST (UTC+10) and AEDT (UTC+11), with daylight saving from the first Sunday in October to the first Sunday in April. That is the northern winter, so its gap with Europe and North America moves by up to two hours during the year. Queensland has no daylight saving, so Brisbane is an hour behind Sydney in summer.
singapore: Singapore stays on UTC+8 with no daylight saving. It moved from UTC+7:30 to UTC+8 at the start of 1982, so older records can look half an hour off.
hong-kong: Hong Kong Time (HKT) is UTC+8 all year, the same clock as Singapore and mainland China. Hong Kong last used daylight saving in 1979.
chicago: Chicago uses Central Time: CST (UTC−6) in winter and CDT (UTC−5) in summer. It is one hour behind New York all year. CST can also mean China Standard Time, so check which one a message means.
shanghai: All of China officially uses one clock, UTC+8, although the country spans about five geographical time zones. In the far west, in Xinjiang, many people keep an unofficial local time two hours behind. China last used daylight saving in 1991.
mumbai: India has one time zone, IST (UTC+5:30), with no daylight saving. Because of the half hour, a meeting on the hour in London, New York or Tokyo falls at half past in Mumbai.
new-delhi: New Delhi uses IST (UTC+5:30), like all of India. The offset comes from a central meridian at 82.5°E, chosen so one clock serves the whole country.
toronto: Toronto uses Eastern Time and changes its clocks on the same dates as New York, so the two cities show the same time all year.
berlin: Germany uses CET (UTC+1) and CEST (UTC+2), the same clock as Paris, Madrid and Rome. Germany was among the first countries to adopt daylight saving, in 1916.
madrid: Most of Spain is at about the same longitude as Britain, yet it uses CET (UTC+1) and CEST (UTC+2). Spain moved its clocks forward to match Central Europe in 1940 and never moved back. The Canary Islands stay one hour behind Madrid.
moscow: Moscow stays on UTC+3 all year. Russia moved to a permanent UTC+4 in 2011, then to a permanent UTC+3 in October 2014. Russia as a whole spans 11 time zones, so a Russian contact may not be on Moscow time.
istanbul: Turkey stays on UTC+3 all year. It stopped changing its clocks in 2016, so its gap with Europe grows by an hour in the European winter.
sao-paulo: São Paulo uses Brasília Time (UTC−3). Brazil ended daylight saving in 2019, so older calendars and devices may still suggest a summer change that no longer happens.
seoul: South Korea uses KST (UTC+9), the same clock as Tokyo, and last used daylight saving in 1988.
auckland: Auckland uses NZST (UTC+12) and NZDT (UTC+13), with daylight saving from the last Sunday in September to the first Sunday in April. It is one of the first major cities to start each new day.
san-francisco: San Francisco uses Pacific Time, the same clock as Los Angeles. It is three hours behind New York all year.
mexico-city: Mexico City stays on UTC−6 all year. Mexico ended daylight saving across most of the country in October 2022, so its gap with US cities now changes when the US changes its clocks.
buenos-aires: Argentina stays on UTC−3 all year and last used daylight saving in the 2008-09 summer.
bangkok: Thailand uses Indochina Time (UTC+7) with no daylight saving, the same clock as Ho Chi Minh City and Jakarta.
cairo: Egypt brought daylight saving back in 2023, so Cairo moves between UTC+2 and UTC+3, and older sources may say otherwise. The working week usually runs Sunday to Thursday.
johannesburg: All of South Africa uses SAST (UTC+2) with no daylight saving. It matches Paris and Berlin during the European summer and is one hour ahead in winter.
lagos: Nigeria uses West Africa Time (UTC+1) with no daylight saving. It matches London during British Summer Time and is one hour ahead in winter.
jakarta: Jakarta uses WIB (UTC+7). Indonesia has three time zones, WIB, WITA and WIT, so a contact in Bali or Papua may be one or two hours ahead.
manila: The Philippines uses Philippine Time (UTC+8) with no daylight saving, the same clock as Singapore and Hong Kong.
kigali: Rwanda uses Central Africa Time (UTC+2) with no daylight saving, one hour behind Nairobi.
luanda: Angola uses West Africa Time (UTC+1) with no daylight saving, the same clock as Lagos.
muscat: Oman uses Gulf Standard Time (UTC+4) all year, the same clock as Dubai. The working week usually runs Sunday to Thursday, unlike the UAE, so check the day as well as the time.
cologne: Cologne uses CET (UTC+1) and CEST (UTC+2), like the rest of Germany, changing on the last Sundays of March and October.
nairobi: Kenya uses East Africa Time (UTC+3) with no daylight saving, the same clock as Addis Ababa.
addis-ababa: Ethiopia uses East Africa Time (UTC+3), but many Ethiopians also use a traditional 12-hour clock counted from dawn, so 7:00 on an international clock is said as 1:00. Confirm which clock a time refers to.
caracas: Venezuela is on UTC−4 with no daylight saving. From 2007 to 2016 it used UTC−4:30, so older schedules can be half an hour off.
ho-chi-minh-city: Vietnam uses Indochina Time (UTC+7) with no daylight saving, so Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi keep the same clock.
hyderabad: Hyderabad uses IST (UTC+5:30), like all of India. Because the UK changes its clocks and India does not, 9:00 in London is 14:30 in Hyderabad in winter and 13:30 in summer.
honolulu: Hawaii uses HST (UTC−10) and does not use daylight saving. Its gap with the US mainland grows by an hour during the mainland's summer time.
